Drawing a conclusion about virus transferal was not difficult at all. So it was a singular entity that passed between gaming accounts and left no residual traces on the source? Unusual, but then again, everything about this situation already was. Whatever its programmed “desire” was, it seemed to fulfill it wholeheartedly. Though, it was hard to believe that just turning off the computer and choosing natural selection was enough to restore Phainon’s laptop to a pristine condition after twenty years of wear and tear. Had its performance been so terrible all this time with the memory card stuffed to the brim with Khaslana’s weird glitches? How did he even get anything done like that? Just another instance of Phainon thinking something detrimental to his wellbeing was actually normal and he just handled it worse than other people. The man was far more resilient than anyone gave him credit for. In the midst of drawing his own conclusions, a teleslate screen was shoved into Mydei’s face. The time read 8:15 AM. Still early enough to get a workout in, if he moved quick enough. Phainon, already accustomed to his desire for routine, pinned Mydei in place. He really could have an iron grip when he was desperate. “Nuh-uh, no running today. We’re eating breakfast together!” “But—” “Honeycakes. Can’t. Go. On. Without. Them.” Titans, he was being a pain today. “Spoiled.” Still, it was the least Mydei could do after suffocating him all night. Nevermind the fact that Phainon could cook just as well—if he insisted on having Mydei’s specialty honeycakes for breakfast, then he’d get just that. He cupped a hand around Phainon’s cheek and placed a fleeting kiss there. Even with morning breath and unkempt hair flying in every direction, the man was too charming to resist. His skin flushed at once, from his collarbones to his ears, and once his arms fell slack, Mydei took the chance to roll off his chest. “Wait, Mydei…” “You wanted this. Now get up.” He ignored Phainon’s sputtered complaints, all too happy to leave the man tripping over himself once again. A little torture never killed anyone. After weeks of eating whatever was within reach or opting for overpriced takeout, it was really good to finally cook again. This was also the most well-rested Mydei felt in ages, not even a hint of drowsiness remaining. Each step he took across the kitchen tiles was pleasantly temperate on his bare feet. He scrubbed his hands clean, slipped on his red chimera-embroidered apron (courtesy of Castorice) and tied his hair back before getting to work. Flour. Sugar. Milk. Eggs. Vanilla. Honey—lots of honey. His recipe veered on the sweeter side due to personal preference. Phainon, in comparison, rarely felt cravings for anything beyond his typical healthy diet of glorified leaves and grass. His “cheat day” requests were usually limited to salted or fried meat and vegetable dishes from his hometown. But here he was, surprising Mydei time and again. He had just finished stirring everything together in the bowl and began to heat the pan when those same strong arms from before wrapped around his torso. “Phainon,” he acknowledged briefly before returning to his craft. The other man just groaned and folded deeper into Mydei’s back, deliberately avoiding the sore spot in the middle that always ached after a long day of work. How gentle he was, often caressing that lopsided birthmark in the same spot while they laid together. Phainon would mouth over it, just light enough to leave prickling bumps upon the skin, and mumble, “Each mark of your pain will be remembered.” A tad dramatic for moderate soreness, but undeniably heartfelt. Now, though… “You’ve gotten slower in the kitchen lately. Feeling your age, Mydeimos?” So he’s back to being a thorn in my side, Mydei mentally sighed. He dropped the whisk into the bowl before he instinctively began brandishing it as a weapon to ward off stray pests from his sacred kitchen. Now on the defensive, he crossed his arms and huffed. “You’re the one who’s feeling their age. That’s the only explanation for your recent midlife crisis.” Apparently his accumulated list of ways to torment Phainon had reached its apex already, because a pair of sharp canines instantly dug into Mydei’s neck like he was seeking blood. He yelped, reaching for the first object in the vicinity, and ended up whacking Phainon like a fly with the batter-coated whisk. It hit him violently in the head, causing him to finally unlatch from Mydei’s nape, and both men groaned in unison. After a moment of staggering, they locked eyes and took the offensive, shoving one another around the edge of a heated stove as globs of their breakfast flew through the air. “You’re such a dog!” “And you’re a brutish cat! My forehead’s going to bruise!” The insults went flying between them too, adding to the growing puddle of filth around them. It was only a short while into their roughhousing, however, that Phainon unexpectedly slipped and instantly took Mydei down with him. They ended up just as they had been positioned before—Mydei sprawled out on top of Phainon, who had willingly taken the brunt of the fall and wheezed out a little as his back hit the floor. “Fool. You should’ve turned away instead of letting me crush you to death,” Mydei chided, smoothing out Phainon’s pinched brow. The other man just laughed. “Ha, no way. Even if I die, my chivalry will outlive me.” Complete nonsense coming from a sleep-rumpled fool covered in raw batter, but his impassioned rhetoric alone was almost convincing. They basked in the sticky atmosphere for a moment, just feeling one another, before Phainon relaxed into Mydei’s hold. “I really missed this.” There they were, wearing their breakfast and sweating on the dirty kitchen tiles like a pair of idiots after an impromptu wrestling session. The pan was still searing nearby and the scent of burning oil was almost acrid. This was hardly the picture of a romantic morning. Somehow though, it fit them just fine. Soon enough, Mydei sat up with a sneer and brushed himself off. It did nothing to cleanse him of the flour clumping in his hair. “I didn’t. My kitchen has been spotless without you throwing all your dishes everywhere.” “Or, it’s spotless because you didn’t cook the entire time I was gone.” Mydei just clicked his tongue, not honoring that provocation with a response. So what if it was true? He’d never admit to it. Phainon, though, was never one to let these things slide. He always bit down hard, too stubborn and too attention-seeking to release him until he got his way. “Hit a nerve, Mydeimos?” “I was just distracted by the batter all over your face. It’s a good look on you.” Their banter continued where it had last left off weeks and weeks ago, as if it had just been stuck on pause the whole time, waiting for them to come back and find their peace with one another. Such was the foundation of their relationship, the way they originally found common ground after months of stagnation once they learned to relate to one another through their physicality. It wasn’t limited to intimate moments either, but shifted over to aggressive competitions when their youthful rage caught up to them. There was that time in Mydei’s fourth year when he was interning at the university library and Phainon dragged him into a ridiculous book-stacking contest that quickly spiraled out of control and almost lost him the job. At the thirty-third book, Phainon’s stack began to sway precariously in either direction, eventually ramming into Mydei’s and sending everything tumbling down to the floor with a loud THUD! The sound was so great a few students in the outer hall complained, leading the head librarian to come chew them out. Mydei, humiliated, kept his eyes steadily on the ground as he groveled before his boss. Kind as the elderly Zenotus was, he could not stand for the blatant disrespect of his books, and thus he ordered Mydei to clean and reshelve every outstanding volume from that week on his own. The task was so tall he had to stay hours past closing each night to make a dent in his workload. Of course, Phainon ended up sneaking in after hours to help. And they only ended up making out in the corner like, two times at maximum. They could be productive when they needed to. In truth, they’d always been just this stupid around one another since the beginning. And no matter how bleak the situation looked, there was the unspoken promise that it would always remain this way. Mydei never thought softness suited him well. He was too big, too gruff, too Kremnoan for the delicate sensibilities of the Okhemans. Not exactly the perfect image of a gentle lover in their eyes. Still, he whispered, “I missed you, too.” And their morning continued as usual. After remaking the batter, sitting down with a stack of honeycakes each, scrubbing his body clean of every speck of wasted food, and pulling on a cardigan and slacks—Mydei was finally ready to leave the house at just after nine-thirty. He set one of his carrying cases down in the kitchen while combing his hair back, walking back and forth between the bathroom and open areas of the apartment in search of all his belongings. He heard Phainon pacing at one point, but he seemed to calm down after a while and took to waiting patiently for Mydei in the sitting room; said patience which seemed to disappear as soon as he laid eyes on the man and shot up from his seat like one of Tribbie’s toy rockets. “Mydei,” he called, “Are you proud of me? I called Cyrene and Castorice, and I also messaged Hyacine and Cipher privately.” It was too early to be proud of him for doing the bare minimum to communicate with his friends of over seven years. All of the girls had known Phainon far longer than Mydei had, and he wasn’t the only one missing him. “And how did that go?” Phainon gripped his teleslate in both hands like a lifeline. “Well…I’m still breathing?” “That’s probably more than you deserve.” Mydei busied himself with his sleeve buttons, ignoring whatever wounded look Phainon cast his way. “Cyrene’s family to you. It’s wrong to cut your family out like that.” That comment earned him a cough in return. He raised a brow and met Phainon’s gradually-reddening face. Another cough, a shifty glance, and then Phainon’s wobbling voice—“Technically that also applies to you. Since we’re, you know.” “Since we’re what?” “Don’t make me say it!” Mydei was in the middle of a definitely-suave, not at all humiliating line when he got a closer look at Phainon’s teleslate. His jaw clamped down immediately, eyes narrowed as the latest search results were displayed for all to see: > does he actually like me or am i delusional > gladiatr > should i quit my job > wovenin upload résumé > how to nonchalantly seduce someone help please Forget the “family” talk, Mydei had more pressing matters to attend to. “Why did you search for ‘gladiatr?’” Phainon didn’t honor him with a response. Not surprising at all. Mydei’s mood continued to sour as he cast a highly judgmental stare his partner’s way. “You have the wrong idea. It wasn't anything serious!” Phainon floundered for the right words, and inevitably said all the wrong ones instead. Mydei, being a rational person, came to understand him rather quickly. But he couldn’t resist the urge to hit Phainon with a few more jabs before their morning together ended. “Hm? So you're willing to leave all this,” he gestured vaguely at the room around him, and then at the leftover stack of honeycakes set out on the counter, which earned him a whimper, “behind for a casual fling?” He then turned and headed towards the front door, paying no heed to Phainon’s brainless attempts at fighting back. Mydei pulled on his coat, secured his usual satchel over his shoulders and reached for the doorknob just slowly enough for Phainon to come barreling into him once more from the side. Round, pleading eyes burned a hole right into his profile. “Where are you going?” And Mydei just couldn’t resist messing with him one final time. He hid his smile and swiveled back to face Phainon head-on, crossing his arms and assuming a bland expression. Perfect. “To work. To pay the bills and afford all these nice ingredients to make dinner for my ungrateful, disloyal husband.” Phainon immediately choked on whatever he was going to say next. He looked ready to explode with how intensely red his face was, and all he did was echo “HUSBAND?” before gaping like a fish out of water. How satisfying to leave him in such a state at the end of all the suffering Mydei had endured. Revenge was easy when your partner was just so easy. Mydei left the apartment then, only pausing briefly by the elevator as he remembered to call out to the wide open door, “Have fun at your little rendezvous. At the end of the day, you'll still be here begging for me anyway.” He was happy to leave it there, firmly securing a victory for himself amid an endless tally of losses. But once again, Phainon would continue to surprise him. “Wait! Don’t leave just yet, I still have to—” He rounded the corner with purpose and stood before Mydei, only an imperceptible bit taller. So his pace was undoubtedly faster now, catching up after hardly any time at all. That was new. What was a self-assured win fizzled into utter nothingness as Phainon held his cheek and leaned in for a honey-sweet kiss, saccharine enough to make Mydei’s heart flutter against his own will. Damn it. Damn it all to Thanatos’ realm. “Have a good day, Mydei.” His tone was gentle and obviously a little proud of himself. Mydei, again at a loss for words, nodded once and backed into the elevator like a lovestruck fool. And he hardly uttered a single word the rest of the morning. At least his productivity was up, having his life balance restored to acceptable levels of rest, relaxation and companionship. Apparently he was basically glowing like a lamp the entire day, so much so that even Krateros muttered not so far behind his back, “I see that ridiculous boy of yours finally came to his senses.” If Phainon had come to his senses then Mydei had clearly lost all of his in the process. Wasn’t that something Professor Anaxagoras taught them back in their student days—that “equivalent exchange” he coveted so greatly? Right, that was it. The concept seemed to apply to all areas of Mydei’s life constantly; exchange your homeland for opportunity, or your honor for social acceptance. That's how it usually was, anyway. The costs were steep, but never too detrimental, given that he benefitted from every outcome. Now it was a little different. Be it your computer for Phainon’s or sleep for the pursuit of truth or even that novel you really needed to return in exchange for a failed opportunity to one-up your partner, he just couldn’t seem to win even once. That trend stretched further into the day as the Parting Hour brought Mydei back to the familiar beige of his apartment building. It was a more attractive sight overall when compared to Phainon’s dingy little place, but the lack of color was too far of a lean in the minimalist direction for Mydei’s tastes. He never did like the gray haze that settled over Kremnos’ industrial scene growing up. The slight chill in the west wind was finally shrugged off along with his overcoat at the front door. His boots and satchel followed, and a minute later, Mydei was treading through the silent expanse of his home exactly as he had each day over the past month. The difference was nearly indiscernible now, save for a few key details: a half-filled coffee cup on the coffee table, the same plate of sad-looking honeycakes sitting atop the counter, and a leather book left wide open on the dining table. Disconcerting. That was all Mydei could think before a clamor came from the office. The door was closed shut, but the noises coming from within were still very audible from the entryway. It sounded like a hard object slamming down onto the desk, followed by the rapid clicking of a keyboard and the sharp hum of electricity. What was Phainon up to now? Still trying to get that résumé uploaded? It shouldn’t be too much of a problem if his laptop was running faster. Mydei pushed the door open with a slight creak, letting in the light cast from the hall into the dim room. There Phainon was, seated at the desktop computer where Khaslana was hovering in place as always, his hand gripped around the mouse like a weapon. Mydei couldn’t make out his expression from the door, but his pale hair seemed to glow from behind. How could a person be so naturally beautiful amidst so much building frustration and anger in their life? The creature seemed to recognize Mydei’s footsteps before Phainon did, and its gaze shifted away from the office chair to the intruder. Somehow, despite wearing the same blank expression as ever, it seemed agitated. “Are you harassing one another now?” Mydei hoped to break the tense air with some easy banter, but it fell flat upon drawing close enough to make out Phainon’s terse glare. Were they really fighting with each other? How did that even work? Now hoping to de-escalate the situation, Mydei forcibly removed the mouse from Phainon’s grasp and placed the nearby glass of water in it instead. “Drink it properly instead of slamming it around,” he ordered. Phainon, probably too far gone to argue, began to sip from the glass. In the meantime, Mydei navigated over to Khaslana’s trembling form and let it hold onto the mouse for emotional support. Once it had calmed down, Mydei decided to probe it for context. “Khaslana,” he said, “can you—” CRASH! Glass shattered all over the floor as the remaining water soaked through the rug and their socks. The sound startled Mydei, but Phainon was frozen in place, his face gaunt and hand still shaking around a nonexistent cup. Concerned, Mydei reached out to check for injuries, but he jerked away instantly like a cornered animal. “What…did you say?” Mydei hadn’t said much of anything with how quickly he was interrupted, but something in there had clearly set Phainon off. He finished his sentence, “‘Khaslana, can you talk to me?’” Phainon took a shuddering breath. “And who…are you talking to?” “The fairy creature. It answers to that name.” He watched Phainon carefully, taking in each rigid pull of his muscles, the way his darkened eyes seemed to blink in and out of focus, the sweat pooling on his hairline and how utterly terrified he looked. It wasn’t just shell-shock from the glass breaking, no. That reaction was undeniable—the name meant something to him too. Mydei spoke again, “Where have you heard the name ‘Khaslana’ before?” “Nowhere.” A clipped, one-word response that was so obviously ingenuine, Mydei barely resisted the urge to reach forward and throttle him. “That was a quick answer.” “Just drop it, Mydei.” How stubborn. Good thing Mydei could be just as bullheaded when it mattered most. He decided to try a new angle of attack next. “That book was left open on the table.” Phainon was all too happy to embrace the sudden shift in topic. With a deceptively light tone, he asked, “What book?” “The 500 year old artifact from the special collections at work. The one that has to be kept in a protective casing at all times.” Phainon nodded sagely. “Ah. That one.” He wasn’t even denying his own oversight now. So out of character. Unimpressed, Mydei continued to implicate him, “You know proper handling procedures better than anyone. Something must have shaken you pretty badly for you to abandon an artifact like that.” “Your friend…” Phainon’s breath was pulled taut with thinly-veiled distress. “‘Khaslana,’ he was acting strange. That’s all.” You’re a poor liar, Phainon, Mydei thought to himself before voicing aloud. He really, truly was. But given his clear misery, he was in far worse shape than he had been the day before. And Mydei was willing to give him more time to come to terms with his issues. As long as they had each other, everything would work out in the end. Right on cue, Phainon began deflecting again. “I don’t know what you’re talking about. Come on, let’s not do this now. No one wants to argue after working all day, right?” He pulled Mydei over the pile of broken glass shards underfoot and began leading him down the hallway. “I think it’s about time for our evening bath!” What else could Mydei do but let himself be whisked away? This abnormal routine continued throughout the week. Phainon seemed reluctant to go home, to part with Mydei at all, but he was just as eager to shoo the man off to work every morning. Each one of his messes had been promptly cleaned up and he was clearly determined to be as unobtrusive as possible. Mydei didn’t catch him unawares in the office room again, but there was no doubt Phainon was still hiding himself away in the darkened room during the day. At least the creature didn’t appear as perturbed compared to the first time they clashed. On one occasion, Mydei found Phainon sprawled out on the sitting room divan reading Origin of Primordial Chaos. His long legs were a sight to behold even beneath those hideous purple lounge pants he was so enamored with. Mydei laid a hand upon his thigh, causing Phainon to glance up curiously from his book. “And here I thought all you read was the monthly edition of Moneymaking for Dummies,” Mydei taunted. He sat beside Phainon and leaned in to check the current page number—forty-nine. It was a relatively short story, but he’d barely made it a fourth of the way through. Seems it really wasn’t to his tastes. “What’s the verdict then?” Phainon grimaced. “I don't typically read stories of this kind.” “Trust me, no one else does either.” The ill-tempered scholar from before was a testament to that. It was for the best that the archival team resolved that request before a repeat incident occurred. “Ha, perhaps. But don't you agree that the text offers unexpected insight into the past?” “In the footnotes and citations?” “In general. Though the execution is questionable, there is merit to his theorems.” Phainon set the book down atop his chest and faced the ceiling as if searching for something beyond anyone’s perception. “Little is known about the chrysos heirs of the prophecy. That shouldn't be though, since they were all local celebrities and several were already legends carved into the history books.” Mydei knew exactly what he was getting at. Among all of Amphoreus’ historians, it was the Flame-Chase fanatics who were most often left unsatisfied by their research results. How could it be that the revered heroes of ancient times were also so neglected by the countless slates, scrolls and doliums alike? How was it that not a single name survived from that era? Surely the people of those times were not so careless as to leave their greatest heroes and deities unnamed, right? Even the power of their combined contemplation could not remedy this problem plaguing the entire world. Sure, they could make an effort— perhaps history was destroyed intentionally by malicious forces like the Cleaners, or followers of the Enigmata were involved somehow. It never amounted to much in the end aside from twin headaches and a disdain for the author’s cryptic thinking. “I mean, Khaos?” Phainon’s brow twitched with some indescribable force of emotion. “This Kryptos is a total lunatic. The obvious Kephale fetish aside, he’s all show and no substance with these naming conventions!” Mydei snorted lightly, “It's a name found throughout Amphoreus' history.” “Then why have I never heard it before? Must not be that important.” “It's important to anyone with a brain, you amateur historian.” Mydei whacked him over the head with a notepad shared during their ruminating. “It’s high time you caught up on your studies.” Thursday in particular was another deviation from the expected, though not because of any great fault on Phainon’s behalf. He was surprisingly active that evening when Mydei found him back at the computer messing around with Khaslana. The man was usually tidy, but the crumbs and wrinkled food wrappers before him told a different story. He was engrossed in a bizarre, disorganized series of web searches, spanning anywhere from salad eating contests to sky castrum mural fragments to best penaconian films where the dog lives. Clearly the prompts themselves were arbitrary and it was the top pages themselves he cared about. Mydei watched in utter silence for minutes on end as Phainon continuously scrolled through hundreds of webpages just to allow tracking permissions from each and every one. After a certain point he pushed off from the wall and drew nearer. “What are you doing to my computer now?” “Mydei!” Phainon cheered with far too much glee. Were those crumbs around his mouth too…? What was he, a toddler? The very grown man in front of him pointed at the pop-up prompt on the screen, exclaiming, “I’m feeding Khaslana cookies!” Mydei pinched his nose. There’s no way… “That’s not—” Mydei cut himself off as he caught a glimpse of the smirk playing at his partner’s lips. Oh, he knew exactly what he was doing. The unkempt scene around him suddenly made a lot more sense. Crumbs and wrappers everywhere? He was causing a scene on purpose. “You really enjoy messing with people.” In a leering voice, Phainon replied,“Hm? What gave it away?” “The fact that you're also eating cookies right in front of Khaslana to taunt him. The same way you hold my hand while he just gets the mouse.” Phainon’s haughty laugh soon followed along with the crumpling of another emptied treat bag. What a way to make the most of his cheat day. “Khaslana's just a string of code simulating life. So I'm giving him some enrichment time to boost his performance capabilities. I'm sure he won't mind too much.” Then, with a scornful grin directed at the screen, he added, “Or you can just think of this as payback for all the havoc you wreaked my entire life. I lost a lot thanks to you, you no-good troublemaker.” It was true enough, but the act was a bit much. Surely there were better things to do around the apartment than wasting his time torturing a character sprite. “I didn’t think your relationship had grown so hostile. Are you that full of hatred, Phainon?” he voiced. “I never said I hated him! I actually like to think Khaslana is very misunderstood.” He seemed to have second thoughts immediately after the words of praise left his mouth. “Except for when he skewered Bubbles. That's an unforgivable sin!” At least he still had some common sense. And there was promise for their relationship to improve now that Phainon had evolved from acts of pure malice to petty taunting. Khaslana was also reacting less as the days went by. It must have been a good sign, like the light at the end of a long tunnel. Friday saw the reunion of their art history group at the Golden Scapegoat Café. Aglaea and Castorice were already sipping from their mugs of herbal tea by the time Mydei and Phainon arrived, wearing a pair of pleased smiles as their more estranged friends approached hand in hand. Tribbie and her sisters, who had yet to outgrow their youthful energy, were excitedly whispering about their extra-special new concoction, “Rainbow Pegasus Bubble Tea.” Hyacine would probably get a kick out of that one. “Mydeimos, Phainon. It’s nice to see you at this early hour,” Aglaea greeted warmly. Her words clearly held some kind of passive-aggressive sleight within them, but no one could manage a frown on such a beautiful morning. The Month of Cultivation always brought a pleasant heat to Okhema’s maze-like streets, pushing away the lingering wisps of winter to embrace the season of flowers. Castorice reserved her words and instead held out her hands over the table to each of them, seeking the comfort of their companionship. The trio shared a private smile together before their young friends came bounding over with drinks in tow. “Snowy! De! You’re back!” The three sisters chimed in unison. Trianne and Trinnon handed over Phainon’s usual coffee order along with Mydei’s juice before heading off on their own. Tribbie sat at the end of the table drinking her own beverage through a yellow, star-shaped bendy straw. Phainon grinned, tilting his head in a way that caused his springy strands of hair to bounce atop his head. “It’s great to finally see you all again.” No matter how much trouble he’d caused before, that energy was impossible to resist. Everyone collectively relaxed into their seats and let the tension of the previous month wash from their bodies. The group talked about this and that, conversing about whatever came to mind as memories from years past came rushing in. “We were in Professor Anaxa’s class together, but while you and Phainon grew closer, I was too shy to introduce myself. Now, I can’t imagine a life where the two of us never became friends.” “It was our first field trip to Mnestia’s Temple, remember? Agy was so focused on the tour that she didn’t even realize her students had gone missing!” “Aglaea had a stern gaze, and Tribbie and Castorice were always working on handicrafts in the corner. Even someone like me would feel a little intimidated when I was just starting out!” “Mydeimos makes a splendid array of fruit tarts. While his unique historical perspectives were certainly a breath of fresh air, it was his talent in the kitchen that first captivated me.” It was all too easy to fall back into an easy rhythm amongst themselves. After an hour of chatting, Mydei felt astonishingly refreshed. Continuing from Aglaea’s last point, Phainon nodded excitedly and added, “That reminds me of the time we had a grand feast all together!” A curious turn in the conversation for sure. Mydei silently racked his brain for any memories relating to feasts. Were communal celebrations counted in that? The group had always attended the Month of Joy’s fish festival to support Mydei’s volunteer work at the dining stalls. There was also the Kremnoan Cultural Center’s open house day in the Month of Strife where he made every traditional dish preserved in the ancient recipe books. Tribbie also seemed to follow his thought process. “Oh, for the Month of Gate’s homecoming rites? De’s pancakes are always the best!” “No, when we all gathered at the bathhouse for that banquet.” At everyone’s lasting silence, he redirected in Mydei’s direction and gestured wildly, stressing, “You know which one I’m talking about, right Mydei? We had that grape throwing competition and you launched one so hard it shattered Professor Anaxa’s glass?” Phainon’s insistence on pushing this topic was honestly puzzling. What was he getting at here? Mydei squinted down at the table, scanning over stray pastry crumbs and coffee stains burned into the wood in hopes of recalling something of value. Feast, bathhouse, grapes… “You made that gorgeous cake, the one with the gold laurels on it?” Now his voice was straining with something like desperation. Mydei, ever the determined man, was so focused on remembering that he had almost completely disconnected from reality. He eventually caught hold of one lead, leaving just one word on the tip of his tongue: …Cake? Strangely, something did come to mind: a rich fig cake dressed in a flawless mirror glaze that reflected every star beyond the sky. It was indeed beautiful, and crowned with edible golden leaves made of lemon wafers. Subtle notes of jam, citrus and vanilla filled Mydei’s senses, just as vibrant as the day he’d baked it. When he snapped back into reality, the group was watching his expectantly, Phainon most of all. It wouldn’t be polite to keep them waiting, he thought to himself, and then finally answered, “Right. It was something for Mnestia. You stayed in the hot baths too long and turned the color of raw dromas meat.” Phainon perked up at that. He nodded repeatedly, eager for acknowledgement, before his brows furrowed and a scowl replaced his smile. “Hey, if I recall correctly you were the one who pushed me—” As if sensing an inevitable battle of words to follow, Aglaea swiftly interjected with her usual grace, “Ahem. If I may…” Her all-seeing eyes shone warily behind the lip of her mug. It was a stance of authority, a promise to correct the unseemly flaws in her students’ work. Mydei was all too familiar with this scenario, and he listened closely, chin lowered out of habit, for the obligatory admonishment regarding their childish behavior. “Perhaps you are both misremembering. No such feast was ever held between us.” What? Tribbie also piped up, her big eyes stretched wider than Amphoreus’ twin moons, “That’s right! We’ve never even been to the bathhouse together!” “Huh?” Phainon wore the look of a man completely dumbfounded. Mydei may well have laughed if he wasn’t frozen in the exact same position. Always the gentle mediator, Castorice was quick to supplement an explanation. “Tribbie and her sisters are still young, and in the past they couldn’t enter the hot baths at all. We’ve only held parties where everyone can be included…” She wore a pensive expression as she tore through her own memories for any small inkling of truth. It seemed to come to her soon enough, and she readily suggested, “The last time we celebrated together was during the new year. Surely you’re confusing that occasion with another…?” A less-than-elegant chortle resounded for a split second. Aglaea always was a woman of mysterious duality. She leaned backwards, satisfied with Castorice’s words, and closed her eyes. “Might I suggest you two spend less time entertaining your drinks next time so you retain some memory of the evening?” Her snippy tone was undoubtedly grating on the ears of such a people-pleasing crowd. Even Castorice, who had received praise for her careful speculation, winced away from the face of this conflict. For as much as Mydei respected her judgment, he wasn’t one to shy in the face of adversity. Being a man of Kremnos meant pursuing the core principles of courage, honor, tenacity, sacrifice and reason to the bitter end —even at the cost of his pride. Not that anything could be more shameful than allowing falsehoods to corrupt history. Amphoreans of all kinds, from every hidden corner of this forsaken world, had nothing but scraps of a plundered past to rely on. Mydei would always strive to ensure that memories remained firmly under his protection. The argument formed like needles on his tongue, “I never—” And was unceremoniously quashed the next second by a harsh stamp of a heel on his toes. Mydei hissed back a curse and glared over at his troublemaking partner, who seemed very inclined to ignore his existence. With a jovial chuckle, Phainon agreed, “Understood. We will definitely be more careful next time!” Mydei shot him a menacing side glance in return. What are you doing? It was pretty common knowledge that neither of them were big on drinking. Mydei disliked the astringent taste of alcohol and very rarely indulged during the occasional birthday celebration or rites of Phagousa. Someone with Phainon’s iron will to keep up appearances also wouldn’t slacken so easily. It was almost insulting to suggest that they could act with such indulgence while hosting a public event. And moreover, Mydei remembered that feast well. Sure, the actual occasion may have been lost on him, but it definitely happened at one point or another within the past half-decade. There was an expertly-crafted cake, sweetened grapes and pomegranate fresh in his mouth, the swirling steam of the hot baths, a sultry whisper smoldering in his ear, “Mydeimos, your body is so unfair,” and the sound of a body being shoved hard into the water. It was something out of a dream, but too real to discount. Becoming too inebriated to recall the details of a party and completely making up the rest was out of the question. But his impassioned disagreement fell to silence in the face of Phainon’s discreet headshake. It told Mydei enough to rein him back in—Not now. Later. Phainon waved off the attention with his natural charm, ceding to Tribbie’s building anticipation of the summer festivities. The conversation slowly waned as Aglaea, Castorice and Mydei watched on without a word, and a shared glance with Phainon pushed him to finally stand and drag the other man home. The pair had opted to walk to the café that morning, hoping to bask in the pleasant weather as they met their daily cardio quota, so Mydei took off down the street with Phainon gripping tight to his bicep. The mood was light enough, not yet dampened by that inexplicable dip in the conversation earlier. But Phainon was looking somewhat worse for wear now that his mask was starting to slip again. His face was slightly pale, resembling the ivory walls between the temple and street more than his bright complexion. If he was coming down with something, Mydei would be sure to take care of him the same way Phainon always cared for him—with unpalatable cough syrup, a cool rag, and a mountain of facial tissues. “You alright?” Phainon hugged his side, a shadow partially obscuring his face from view. He seemed in good enough spirits, just…a little distant. Like his mind was wandering the stars as his body remained firmly within reach. “I’m fine. Really, just having you by my side is more than enough.” Mydei leaned close to ruffle his hair, earning himself a gasp of false outrage. When he pulled back, Phainon’s cloud of white hair was sticking up in every direction. It reminded him somewhat of Khaslana’s unruly mop. The uncanny parallels between those two just never ceased. “You’ve been laying it on thick all week. Are you still not satisfied with the attention you’re getting?” Phainon hummed and knocked his very unbruised forehead—no, the whisk was never going to leave a dent when he was the one constantly ramming into things on his own—against Mydei’s. “Looks like I just can’t get enough of you, Mydeimos. Would you keep indulging me? Of course he would. Wasn’t that the entire point? “Could you get my pullover while you’re in there? The black one? Thanks.” Phainon’s voice drifted into the bedroom from his perch over in the office. Mydei, who was already rummaging around through the cabinets searching for fever reducers, easily complied. Phainon was already looking a little clammy after the journey home and was obviously in need of assistance. Mydei didn’t even know he owned a black pullover, but whatever. It was a fair deal for the rancid medicine he’d soon be force-feeding the man. He pored through his closet (their wardrobes were distinct, but intertwined nonetheless), sifting through each hanger and pile of folded clothes searching for the requested article. White button-downs, gray sweats, fuzzy animal pajamas… Phainon had enough junk piled in there to comfortably live off without ever returning to his own apartment. Mydei let out a satisfied noise as finally dug up the tattered hoodie from the very back of his storage shelves. It might’ve smelled a little like dust and years of neglect, but it was strangely familiar all the same. He called out, “Found it. Do you want me to—?!” What interrupted him this time was a blaring alarm sound so excruciatingly loud Mydei recoiled from the opposite side of the hallway. It had to be an error alert emanating from the computer, from something that set the little virus off. He was more concerned about whether Phainon’s hearing was still intact after enduring that kind of shock, since he had reacted so poorly in the past. Mydei entered the office and his eyes immediately flew to Phainon’s distressed figure hunched over in front of the screen. The room was so bright, flooded with flickering light cast from what could only be Khaslana, and stifling enough to fill his lungs with distressing heat. It was the same scorching haze the creature emitted the first and only time Mydei had attempted to forcibly shut it down. The computer’s fans were set to an impossible speed, adding an extra layer of noise atop the continuous error windows popping up. Phainon wasn’t covering his ears this time, though; instead, he was gripping the mouse with incredible force as sweat poured down his face. He was incredibly pale, blanched by the increasing strain upon his body. Once Mydei reached him, he made out the man’s pinched expression— completely concentrated in enduring whatever pain he was currently experiencing. The exact same expression that Khaslana now wore. The creature was set in a violent fury, its decaying form thrashing and glitching around the screen as a trail of black cubes cast a shadowy void all around. Each time it moved, the cracks etched into its snow-white skin seemed to grow, and the golden blood was inverted to a deep purple hue. It was a complete amalgamation of its former glory, twisting a regal, angelic body into something more sinister. It almost reminded him of… Phainon gasped between labored breaths, “Mydei.” His hands flew to support his partner, who already looked on the verge of collapsing. Phainon’s skin was so hot to the touch, Mydei began to consider calling for an ambulance. How had a fever this high come on so suddenly with such little warning? If he didn’t know any better, he would’ve thought Phainon had fallen into a boiling hot bath again. Between his worrying, he happened to glance up at the monitor again, and a new window caught his eye. It read “⬛️⬛️⬛️δ_me13⬛️⬛️Scepter⬛️Shutdown⬛️⬛️” and a process was currently initiating below: >⬛️Deleting⬛️⬛️⬛️43%⬛️⬛️ >⬛️Del⬛️et⬛️ing⬛️⬛️58%⬛️⬛️⬛️ >⬛️D⬛️el⬛️etin⬛️g⬛️65⬛️%⬛️⬛️⬛️ >⬛️⬛️D⬛️⬛️e⬛️le⬛️ti⬛️n⬛️g⬛️77⬛️⬛️%⬛️ >⬛️⬛️⬛️⬛️⬛️⬛️⬛️⬛️89⬛️%⬛️ >⬛️⬛️⬛️⬛️⬛️⬛️⬛️⬛️99.99%⬛️⬛️⬛️ >⬛️Loading…⬛️⬛️⬛️⬛️⬛️⬛️⬛️⬛️⬛️⬛️ The number was frozen at 99.99% progress. It refused to advance, and the little virus continued to screech out in agony. The creature had reacted poorly when the entire computer was shut down before, but this ‘deleting’ process was only within a single program. Could it be, then, that Phainon had…? “End it,” Phainon begged. His voice was incredibly weak, as if he were just barely holding on to consciousness. “Let go, Khaslana.” If Mydei squinted, he could just barely glimpse the mouse pointer still clutched in the creature’s hands, as if it was still holding on to someone’s hand in its dying moments. That must be what was halting the process, then. It was Khaslana’s will to never let go. The situation was far beyond his comprehension. But even so, Mydei knew what to do. Gently, he removed the mouse from Phainon’s hand and turned it off, just as he had before. The torrent of glitching masses surrounding the creature seemed to multiply exponentially as it wailed and tore at its hair with a pair of crumbling fists. If a computer program could feel emotion, then it was probably enduring an unbearable amount of torture from this deletion process. “I’m sorry. It’ll be over soon,” Mydei soothed the two individuals beside him. His hands shook as he powered the mouse back on and quickly pressed the PERMANENTLY DELETE prompt in the middle of the screen. And Khaslana, in its final moments of anguish, slowly began to fade away in a cloud of darkened ash. He let the dying creature hold his ‘hand’ as it disappeared. And then the screen blinked out to a vacant black space. An ending like this could only throw Mydei’s heart into turmoil. What had even happened here? What had Phainon done, and just what did Khaslana’s reaction mean? He meant to ask the man about his intentions, but a solid THUD! upon the floor suspended his concern about the computer for now. He called out, “Phainon!” but received no response. In the midst of his delirium, he’d fainted to the ground and fallen into a deep, unstirring sleep. His flesh was still heated to a concerning degree. It was time to get him some much-need medicine and rest, alright. And hopefully the situation wouldn’t worsen any more than it already had. Mydei was still perfectly rigid in his bedside seat when Phainon opened his eyes that evening. His fever had mostly subsided and some color had been restored to his face, those sallow lines giving way to a healthier glow already. Even drenched in sweat and bruising around the eyes, he was beautiful. He was typically the pinnacle of health, so the quick rebound wasn’t too unexpected. Whatever this affliction was, it couldn’t have been a typical illness. In all likelihood, it was some kind of stress-induced flareup that would be over with come morning. “You’re awake. Good.” Mydei kept his tone civil, unwilling to place any further stress upon Phainon. No indication of a response was given, but he was willing to be patient. Whatever had occurred that afternoon had unsettled both of them, and they needed time to process everything. He offered a water glass, which Phainon did not take, and then promptly lifted it to the man’s lips without any room for argument. “Hydration is key to recovery. Drink up.” Phainon obeyed, leaning forward to steadily drain the glass until it was emptied. He managed a grateful half-smile and sank back down into the pillows, exhausted by even the smallest movement. Mydei would have been content to let him sleep through the night, but as he turned away, a shaky hand suddenly found his. “Don’t go,” he rasped. “Please.” Under any other circumstances, Mydei would’ve been surprised by how direct his words were. Rarely did Phainon ever express his vulnerabilities outright, much less dare to seize anything for his own benefit. Even in shared moments of affection between them, he’d sooner force Mydei to pursue his own desires, letting go far too soon no matter how desperately he wanted to hold on. Now, though… “Fine.” Mydei didn’t just remain in place, though. He sidled up to the opposite end of the bed and crawled in beside his partner, tugging him in close enough that his tousled hair fell in waves over Mydei’s shoulder. Strawberry-blonde and white strands mingled and intertwined across a shared pillow, just as their bodies melded together like perfect complements in their bed. They would eventually breach the topic of what had truly occurred that evening. It was a conversation that could be put off but never dismissed, just as everything between them was. But all of that was better left for a day free of pain and confusion. Until they could come to terms with all the remaining heaviness lingering in the atmosphere, it was probably better to let it rest. Just as always, Mydei fell into Phainon, into the golden sun seared on his skin that burned hotter than any distant star beyond the sky. Titans, he was so warm. It was simple, existing beside him without needing anything else in return. This shared heat between them, undeniable proof of the life blooming within them, was more than enough. Chapter 7: Epilogue - Eden All throughout Phainon’s life, he had the vague feeling that something, imperceptibly, was wrong. He remembered being five years old, wide-eyed, running through the comforting wheat fields of his hometown wielding a hoe as a sword. None of the villagers were well-off, but that year his parents had bought a brand new laptop to encourage his interest in the world beyond Aedes Elysiae. Cyrene’s storybooks had already inspired something within him, and they made a pinky-promise to one day venture beyond the farthest mountains and trees together. Maybe then, he’d be able to fill that hole within his heart. The gift had excited him at first. He was a little less excited when he learned just how difficult using electronic devices could be. Coming from a traditional farming civilization mostly untouched by the outside world, few people in the village owned teleslates or computers, much less the newest models on the market. He couldn’t read the user manual on his own either, so Phainon could only hope for the best as he tried to learn all its functions on his own. Over time he became proficient in navigating the World Wound Web (after informing his parents that they needed to purchase a home router for browsing purposes) and successfully downloaded his first gaming application NovaNymphs. This was the origin of all his troubles, the very first heartbreak he’d experience as a child. Because only seven days later, he was met with the first of many error messages: The following account has been suspended: Snowy496 Needless to say, once he realized that his beloved virtual puppy was gone forever, Phainon cried and cried like never before. “It’s not fair,” he blubbered into his mother’s blouse, smearing snot and tears everywhere. It really, really wasn’t. Even days later, after Phainon’s parents did everything within their power to cheer him up—excusing him from school, making his favorite honey suncakes with venison, letting him run around for an extra hour with Cyrene as they searched for fairies in the woods—a lingering feeling of unease remained within him. Phainon didn’t think he did anything wrong. He may not have been that good with technology, but he tried his best to follow the rules: no talking to strangers online, no sharing his personal information, and no downloading any strange files. So why did it still end up this way? What went wrong along the way? Many years later, in the aftermath of a grueling situation involving two infected computers, a sentient virus and a complete reconstructing of his perceived reality, the answers he once chased relentlessly finally appeared before him. It’s just that… Well. Now that the truth, or at least a part of it, had come to light, he felt more disconnected from his life than ever. And not in the same way when he was desperately running, hoping to find a shred of self-worth by throwing himself headfirst into work and neglecting his personal obligations until he was so winded they overtook him. One Phainon had come to terms with his own value to other people, he had easily fallen back into the roles of friend, student and lover. He no longer saw it as indulgence, but an integral part of his life that should not be discarded. That in itself was a huge hurdle to overcome, and only with patience and fiery tenacity did he finally make the leap. Weeks before the vicious end of all rationality, upon discovering that his laptop had finally been restored to perfect working condition, he made the decision on his own to stop idling around waiting for a miracle to save him. Phainon put in his two weeks’ notice that same morning, determined to leave behind an unsatisfying job and realign his life. His boss, Cerydra, was never impressed with his half-hearted dedication to the business, and naturally she eyed him in that terrifying way no woman of her stature should ever be able to. “Dearest disloyal subject, what do you plan to do now that you’ve plunged your sword deep into our hearts?” Phainon frantically searched for the right words, hoping not to infuriate her any more than he already had. Fortunately, her partner decided to break the silence with a thoughtful hum of appreciation. “I think this sunfish was always destined for greater things beyond the world of salads, Cerydra.” The woman relented at her words, more eager to please a lover’s fantasies than waste time arguing with an average minimum-wage employee who was ready to bolt. Phainon went through his remaining shifts with that question nagging incessantly in the back of his head. What did he plan to do now? In truth, he never wanted anything in particular for himself. He never had any wishes, no long-lasting desires that he was willing to take hold of for his own gratification. The natural response within his heart was something along the lines of I want to help people. But such vague responses rarely moved others. So, he never answered. After his final day of work, Phainon curled up in bed, breathing in the lingering traces left behind in one of Mydei’s old sweaters. More often than not he smelled like wood and citrus, along with the fragrance of old books that clung stubbornly at his skin. It wasn’t like the endless wheat fields and salty ocean breeze of his hometown, but something still familiar and comfortable. Something that was still undeniably home. “I pretended to be strong on my own again just so you all wouldn’t worry. And look how well that’s done for me so far,” he confessed under the secrecy of his sheets, utterly alone in his apartment. “I don’t have a dream of my own yet.” He went for a long, listless walk that same evening, taking in the sights of Okhema in early spring just as a passing traveler would. The difference rested in his memories associated with every street corner, temple, and market stall. That’s our favorite café, he’d think as the thick aroma of coffee beans wafted in his direction. This is where Tribbie failed me for the fifth time during my practice driving exam. There’s the bench where Castorice used to crochet and watch me play basketball. Hours into the night, as Phainon stepped out of the shadows and arrived at Theosphere Lake, the resounding silence seemed to consume him entirely. Dawncloud was largely an administrative district and cultural site, so its steep roads were practically deserted come the arrival of the Curtain Fall Hour. The refined stonework was always technically impressive to gaze upon, but it did little to stir something dormant within him now. All Phainon could do was look up at the statue of Kephale the Worldbearer and drown in his misery as a steady rain began to fall overhead. Coming back to Mydei was just as natural as breathing. That wasn’t any problem he couldn’t handle. What Phainon didn’t know how to deal with was their little uninvited guest. It was a computer virus taking on the form of an angel (not an elf or a fairy, obviously those were completely different), which in itself was so ironic he felt close to tears. Add in the fact that this thing was apparently responsible for every technological failing Phainon had experienced over the course of twenty years, and well—no, of course he wasn’t handling it well. Once they had become acquainted, it was easy to see that he, the creature, was a jealous little imp who had staked his own claim on Mydei despite Phainon’s very clear territorial line already being mapped out in plain sight. He was always reaching for Mydei’s hand, always messaging Mydei from Phainon’s TKQ account, and monopolizing all of Mydei’s time unfairly. Having already been deprived of time with his…partner, Phainon was already at his boiling point. The worst of it came when the two of them were left alone. He refused to cooperate with Phainon, never answering any of his questions and just drifting off to sleep as if everything was uninteresting once Mydei went off to work. Frustrated, Phainon stalked around the apartment searching for something more exciting to play with as the slow hours of the afternoon passed by. It didn’t take long to stumble upon the shiny carrying case Mydei had accidentally left in the kitchen that morning. Phainon wasn’t usually the type to pry, but he recognized this as one of the cases Mydei reserved for transporting artifacts from the archives. Maybe there were treasures inside waiting for appraisal, he reasoned, and popped the silver lock open. Origin of Primordial Chaos wasn’t what he expected in the slightest. It was an unimpressive and thin tome, dressed in leather that had to be centuries old and carrying the stench of dust along with it. Its contents left him in a similar state of dissatisfaction; what was all this nonsense about divine offspring and the overwhelming veneration of Kephale? It was one thing to admire the titans, but this Kryptos was more of a cultist than a reliable source of holy wisdom. The only thing that really stuck with him was that name—Khaos. It was oddly familiar. And so was the appearance of that character. For better or worse, all he could think about was the irritating little creature stuck behind the computer screen. So he returned to the office, started picking another fight with the fickle angel, and nearly lost himself in a strange fit of passionate rage he hadn’t felt in quite some time. He was already close to bursting. And then Mydei walked in, and called out, “Khaslana,” and something broke within him. The shattered glass on the floor was nothing in comparison to how his heart felt. Why is he calling him by that name? Why isn’t it me? Learning that the computer virus that had been not-so-quietly haunting him for pretty much his entire life had also stolen his own name was just downright offensive. But what he felt at that moment wasn’t just anger or hatred, no. It was fear. That was the response his brain had formulated on its own, and trying to make any sense of it was impossible. For some inexplicable reason, Phainon was afraid of the creature. That feeling continued through the passing days in spite of his efforts to overcome it. He reread that lackluster novel and tried to connect the dots between the protagonist and this so-called “Khaslana,” but nothing seemed to fit cleanly. Countless theories floated around aimlessly in his mind: Khaslana : Golden Blood Golden Blood : Kephale Kephale : Khaos Conclusion: Kephale = Khaos = Khaslana? That wasn’t going to cut it. And no matter how he probed Khaslana, tearing through thousands of web pages to capture the creature’s attention and possibly incite some level of communication between them, he never responded. Taunting the little angel was the only way he knew how to deal with his stress. He could feel his body growing weaker as time went on, but at the moment it only seemed to be the result of his tireless efforts. How could he have possibly known what was in store for him? That café date with the art history group was supposed to be a relaxing, freeing experience for all of them. But once his memories were called into question, Phainon felt himself grow tired. He shut down Mydei’s arguments, wanting to leave the morning on a good note without the weight of his wrongness dragging the mood down. His energy continued to deplete as they walked home, and soon Phainon began to feel faint. There was an itching in the back of his mind, a mystical sense that he had to get to the computer, he had to reach it before it was too late. So he sent Mydei away in search of a probably-nonexistent article of clothing that had gotten mixed up in all his mismatched memories. The room was blinding when he stepped inside. Khaslana was waiting for him there, wrapped in a strange golden shell resembling an egg or cocoon. Phainon reached a trembling hand forward and touched the screen, knowing that his touch could never be felt. And yet, that action seemed to make it all the more real. “I’m going to override you now,” Phainon promised the creature as his mouse pointer hovered over the new uninstall prompt onscreen. A mass of chaotic matter surrounded Khaslana in an instant, and Phainon’s head throbbed with an excruciating pain just as a distant alarm began to ring out. He was no longer himself. He was… Mydei’s hands were always soft and warm, but they had turned to ice against his sweltering skin. Whatever words spilled from his mouth in the following moments weren’t his own. They came from him—the other him. And then, with the breath completely knocked from his lungs, he plummeted face-first upon the earth. Phainon appreciated Mydei’s patience with him after this entire mess finally started to fade away, he really did. Titans knew how the man still put up with him after all this time. Before, Mydei had outright told Phainon about his desire to talk about all their issues rather than bottling everything up to the point of exploding, and the sentiment was shared between them. But finding the right words to express every single emotion pounding away within his brain. How could I ever tell you the truth? He wondered day in and out, trying to come to terms with his own uselessness. It was a truth too heavy for even Phainon to bear; those strange, nonexistent memories only came to him in shattered fragments now, as if his mind was trying to shield him. Logically, he knew that Mydei would be able to handle it. The man was headstrong beyond words and, somehow, also bore certain recollections of the past that he shouldn’t have been able to. Still, none of that changed the basis of his predicament. Sometimes Phainon would talk to the mirror in the middle of the night, searching for any remaining trace of golden blood upon his skin. But it would always reflect back flawlessly, no longer the face of a burning idol, but that of a normal young man with a normal life. “This is everything you wanted, you know,” Phainon reprimanded himself as he covered an eye with the hood of his black pullover. And it was, really. But even as the dark circles began to fade and his energy slowly recovered, he was still at a loss for what to do with himself. Could he even live with the weight of an immutable past constantly dragging him down? One day he sat before his laptop, head in hands, trying his best to not fall apart in the face of something so mundane as his WovenIn profile. “I can do just about anything I set my mind to, so a rewarding career is never too far out of reach!” He tried to encourage himself, scrolling through the recent job listings for the nth time that month. “Hmm…let’s see. Local postings only, nothing too far off from Okhema. Commuting is a hassle when you only have two wheels. Oh, and it can’t be minimum wage anymore. It’s exhausting being the only money-strapped person in an otherwise wealthy friend group.” Well, Cipher excluded. She preferred to shirk Aglaea’s comfortable fortune for her own wiles. He groaned, “Only forty results? In all of Okhema? I didn’t think the economy was this bad!” He’d once lived through the end of the world thirty million times over, and it really couldn’t get any worse than that. It’s hard to believe he once lost his mind working a minimum-wage job at a salad bar. “Florist…online gaming technical support…head chef…librarian. Ugh, I’m definitely not qualified for any of these. Oh, a customer representative—for the IPC’s Marketing Development Department? No thanks.” None of these jobs were really rewarding, though. Once upon a time in a completely different age he had been a hero, so the goal of helping people was completely ingrained in his soul. The phantom scars of the past were all but forgotten to Amphoreus now, but there was always someone out there who needed saving. Even if his efforts proved futile over and over again, Phainon was never the type to relent to fate. He had lived a good life this time around. Quiet, unassuming, comfortable, and full of such overwhelming love he’d never fully be able to comprehend. It was funny to think he’d once been denoted as nothing more than an entity of pure hatred and rage. Those feelings were more prevalent once the memories of the past merged with him, but the ability to be a real, living person was freeing. Thinking more about the precious experiences of this lifetime, one thing did come to mind. He murmured to himself, “Teaching wouldn’t be half bad. When I was little, I always assumed I’d take over for Mrs. Pythias one day. Obviously that didn’t end up working out, but there will always be people to teach somewhere.” He drew a hand over his face, trying to contain the small smile threatening to break through. No use in getting too excited this early on. Besides… “Going back to school would be a bit of a drag though. Professor Anaxa’s already more than exhausted of me by now. At least Aglaea would write a thorough recommendation letter if I asked.” Phainon absently played with the strings of his hoodie. “What would I even teach anyway? Art history? Would people really pay to learn from me?” He could almost see it now: all the pains of coming up with lesson plans, wanting to pull out his hair at every incorrectly cited source on students’ papers, sleepless nights where he almost dreaded having to face the people he vowed to instruct. It wasn’t an easy career to pursue by any means, and Phainon lacked the self-esteem to have any faith in his own abilities. However, just as clearly, another vision came into view; his everyday life with Mydei. It was their café dates, mornings spent analyzing ancient artifacts over tea and honeycakes, spending the afternoon away before coming back home to the warm embrace of his person. Inevitably, Phainon spent much of his time fantasizing about the unattainable life he’d always dreamed of having. And now that he was in the midst of living it, he had a difficult time accepting that it was, in fact, real. Was it even plausible? Would Mydei want the same thing as him? Their relationship had always been all over the place, whether he considered all the countless lifetimes of bloodshed or the repression that silenced both of them in this new world. All the time they spent together was proof enough of Mydei’s commitment to him, but he couldn’t help but doubt himself anyway. Was he even cut out for this? It wasn’t that Phainon was unused to wanting things. He was only human, after all. But when it came to actually pursuing those wants? He wasn’t so good at following through. He was always better at making other people happy. Coming to Okhema was Cyrene’s idea in the first place. He just tagged along. And he definitely never meant to settle down here—but who ever prepares themself for love? At the end of the day, whatever Phainon decided, failure was never an option for him. He would commit to his cause without faltering even once. The day he finally began to open up to Mydei was also the day he decided to unveil the fruits of his second high-priority project. It was already well into the Month of Everday when his secret commission was completed, and Phainon was all-too enthusiastic to show it off the minute it fell into his hands. “This is…” Mydei’s voice wavered as he stared in disbelief at the computer screen. It was a familiar expression, all slack in the jaw and with eyes blown up like a bug’s. Phainon just laughed and nudged him forward to grab the mouse. There, hovering on the screen, was another very familiar face. Two pairs of golden eyes interlocked as if they had never been apart. Phainon, now considering himself to be in-tune with his emotions, didn’t bother with envy this time. He just happily exclaimed, “Your brand new desktop assistant— Khaslana! Subscription and spyware-free, of course. It's really just a harmless little guy.” “You made this?” Phainon scoffed. Him, doing anything related to technology? Whatever his natural prowess for data may have been in an era long past was obviously no more in this world. “Not on my own. You may recall that I'm not exactly the most tech-savvy person out there, so I commissioned one of Castorice’s online friends who’s a game developer. All I did was send over the references for his model and animations.” Then, smiling once again, he added, “Truthfully, I knew how fond you'd grown of your little friend. It must be a little lonely when I'm not around, so I wanted to make sure you were always in good company.” Was that a self-compliment? It’s not like Mydei would know even if it was. But as if sensing something was amiss, the man turned to scrutinize him with fiercely focused eyes. “And exactly how much did you spend on this little project?” Ah. He was done for. “...Only about 7500 credits. Plus a 1000 credit tip.” “Phainon, will you ever stop wasting your money on trinkets?” Rude, rude Mydei. How ungrateful could he be? Phainon retorted, “They're antiques, not just some dollar store junk! And neither is Khaslana!” He leaned close to the screen, flashing his most pleading expression Mydei’s way. “How can you look into those big, beautiful eyes and call him useless?” Khaslana’s eyes were indeed far more full of life now that he was just an average virtual assistant instead of a piece of malware simmering inside his hard drive. As if sensing Phainon’s desire for attention, Khaslana instantly summoned Bubbles the Chimera from the void and let the little pet drop onto his spiky hair. He blinked and looked around innocently, swaying under the creature’s weight before smiling slightly. “...You're both using the chimeras against me now?” “It's fair game. See, you're already smiling more. I knew you wouldn't be able to resist him!” Mydei’s gorgeous smile was a sight to behold. He’d been expressing his happiness more openly ever since they had reconciled, and Phainon had already vowed to never forsake his trust again. Mydei sighed, letting go of his concerns to fully appreciate this act of kindness. “Although I question your common sense sometimes, I know you're always genuine. So…thank you.” Phainon just grinned in return before turning back to the screen, chiming, “Look, Khaslana sent you a message!” Khaslana: I grant you a dawn where all spam mail burns to ash! “He's surprisingly diligent.” “Right?” Phainon practically had stars in his eyes. Mydei had once told him how fortunate he felt to have Phainon in his life, how he always felt incredibly warm around him, like a gentle ray of sunlight had descended upon him from beyond the depths of the evernight. He’d once felt conflicted about those words, never knowing how to reply without being consumed by his predecessor’s grief. Now, though, it was starting to feel straightforward enough. He knew just what to say when Mydei later asked him that question, “Don't you ever want to see the worlds beyond?” A smirk rose on Phainon’s lips, playful enough as he stroked at Mydei’s jawline. “No need. You already know how to take me to the stars and back whenever I want.” “Always so crass.” Still, it earned him a half-satisfied sigh that set his heart at ease. Mydei always seemed half-convinced that he was ready to bolt at any given moment, taking off in a rocket ship until their world was just a speck of dust in the corner of his eye. It was stupid; sure, it was interesting to learn about other worlds, but what could Phainon possibly gain from leaving? Before those memories were passed onto him, he didn’t really think about outer space often, aside from treating it as some vague unknown. It was just like Amphoreus’ past, in a way. Phainon always knew in his heart that the truth was out there somewhere, sailing around in the swirling river of time like a drift bottle. He never thought he would be the one to uncover it, though. It didn’t seem possible for someone like him to achieve much of anything. He was just a nobody who worked at a local food chain and hadn’t put his art history degree to any use. It was just collecting dust on a shelf next to those paper tarot cards he and Cyrene had made as kids. Fate, it seemed, was never aligned in his favor. Now, though—now. Even with mere fragments of the past clutched in his freshly cleaned hands, he recognized that this was his perfect second chance. It wasn’t an unending redo of days past in a cycle of violence and flames anymore, but a complete restarting of their lives. Now, he had the chance to do what he had always secretly desired, say what words were always fighting to remain buried beneath the surface. He didn’t need to go anywhere else to become a so-called hero. In a way, everything he’d ever desired was already within reach. The dream of tomorrow, of carrying everyone else’s dreams on to a world free of suffering, was nearly complete. There was only one thing he had left to achieve—a simple wish to stand face to face, free of all masks and no longer held back by the cruelty of the past. So without any restraints to bind him, Phainon leaned ever closer. “Mydeimos…” his breath was hot against the shell of his ear. “I really do love you.” And gods above, did Mydei already know. It was whispered on rare occasions of indulgence as he was lost in a slightly-drunken revelry of unending joy, or during the heights of passion when they were completely unleashed and no longer thinking straight, or in the early hours of the morning when the only words he could manage were against that birthmark in the middle of Mydei’s back. It was in every unspoken word, every time his eyes dripped with unbridled affection, and every time their lips bloomed into a perfect pair. It was everywhere, spreading all throughout his life. And he simply said, “I love you, too,” before they shared in an embrace that would never end. enjoyed their work!

When Mydei finally emerges from the Sea of Souls after nine harsh winters, the most precious thing in the world to him isn’t his name, his body or his life.
